input.quote: Section 7.1 No Resignation. The Servicer will not resign as Servicer under this Agreement unless it determines it is legally unable to perform its obligations under this Agreement.
input.rationale: The Agreement runs until the last Receivable is paid in full or the Issuer is terminated (Section 8.3), a multi-year term. Our only exit is cause-based: under Section 7.2(c) the Servicer may be removed solely "[i]f a Servicer Termination Event occurs and is continuing", and no at-will or convenience termination right exists anywhere for the Issuer or Depositor, who are the customer side here. The Optional Acquisition and Optional Redemption in Sections 8.1 and 8.2 are conditional Class A Certificateholder options (10% pool threshold; February 2021 date plus Make-Whole Payment; Administrator consent), not a customer convenience right. That is the walk-away case of no customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months, so the fallback is not met on its material terms. The Vendor side already exceeds both levels: Section 7.1 bars the Servicer from resigning except on legal inability, so that preferred element is already met and is left untouched (moving to the fallback would hand the Servicer an end-of-term convenience right it does not have). I therefore target preferred and insert only the missing customer convenience right, numbered Section 7.2A so Article VII cross-references stay clean. The new termination is a termination "under this Agreement", so it feeds the existing Section 7.4 Successor Servicer machinery; Section 7.3 confirms effectiveness is "the date stated in the notice of termination" and is not conditioned on a Successor Servicer accepting engagement, so the 30-day notice operates as drafted. Servicing Fees are payable in arrears on each Payment Date, so the refund limb is protective only.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.

proposal.summary: Add numbered Section 7.2A giving the Issuer (as customer) a convenience termination right on 30 days' notice with pro rata refund of prepaid Servicing Fees
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have no right to exit this servicing arrangement other than for a Servicer Termination Event, so we add a new Section 7.2A allowing us, as the customer under this Agreement, to terminate for convenience on thirty (30) days' written notice with a pro rata refund of any prepaid Servicing Fees. Section 7.1 already prevents the Servicer from walking away mid-term, so no change is needed there; we can discuss a longer notice period if that is easier.

ops.text: Section 7.2A Termination for Convenience. The Issuer, as the customer under this Agreement, may terminate this Agreement, and the Servicer's rights and obligations under this Agreement, for convenience and without cause, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the Servicer, and the Servicer will refund, pro rata, any Servicing Fees paid in advance for any period after the effective date of the termination.
